subject: Private Offer: tiered-duration pricing + delegated buyer approvals
messages:
From: Alexandra Bates <alexandra.bates@acmeretail.com>

Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com

Subject: Re: Private Offer: tiered-duration pricing + delegated buyer approvals

Hi Chloe / Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme's platform team liked the latency benchmarks. Procurement asked us to confirm two things before we can move to legal: 1) can Redwood structure the private offer with two term lengths (12 and 36 months) with different unit pricing, and 2) can we delegate sign-off for purchases under $150k to Acme business owners (i.e., not require centralized procurement approval)?

If you can send a short one-page summary of the pricing tiers and the proposed buyer authorization flows, procurement will queue this for their next committee meeting on Oct 8.

Alexandra
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Retail

Attachment: none (will accept your summary PDF)

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Alexandra Bates <alexandra.bates@acmeretail.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: tiered-duration pricing + delegated buyer approvals

Alexandra — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers below and I attached a short summary PDF and the procurement checklist for your committee.

1) Pricing tiers: we can publish one private offer with two SKUs: RDW-STD-12 (12mo) and RDW-ADV-36 (36mo). Suggested list pricing: $0.095/token for 12mo, $0.075/token for 36mo (volume bands apply). We can also set a soft floor so discounts don’t stack beyond agreed bands.

2) Delegated approvals: Marketplace private offers require the buyer's marketplace admin to accept the PO. However, we can implement a delegated internal approval policy on Acme's side: any purchase < $150k can be approved by a designated Acme BU lead and the marketplace purchase executed by your procurement team as an admin. We can capture the delegated approver email addresses in the private offer metadata to help with audit trails.

Next steps: I propose a short pilot — 36mo SKU for a single BU with a $100k initial commit and delegated approver list; if the committee approves, legal + marketplace PO setup can follow.

Attached: RDW-Acme-private-offer-summary.pdf, acme-procurement-checklist.xlsx

—
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: RDW-Acme-private-offer-summary.pdf (2 pages), acme-procurement-checklist.xlsx (3 sheets)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: tiered-duration pricing + delegated buyer approvals

Chloe — nice summary. A few internal notes before we send final copy to Acme:

- Pricing: confirm that the 36mo list price assumes annualized commit and we reserve the right to reprice at renewal (we should call this out).
- Marketplace constraints: AWS requires the buyer's account to accept the private offer and the PO to be linked to the private offer ID. Any delegated approver approach has to be formalized on Acme's side; we can support by adding a buyer-approver field in the offer metadata but AWS won't accept transactions from non-admins.
- Legal: request redlines for the offer terms (attach redlines_v1.docx).

Can Karthik outline the minimal marketplace metadata we need from Acme (account IDs, list of approver emails, initial PO amount)? I want to avoid back-and-forth with their procurement committee.

V

Alexandra — appreciate the quick turnaround and the roster. We can accommodate the $200k delegated approval threshold with one caveat: Redwood needs the marketplace admin(s) to execute the private offer acceptance; the delegated approver field will be recorded for your internal audit and we will surface it in our Console for traceability.

Operational checklist for acceptance (what AWS marketplace will need):
- Buyer AWS Account ID(s) (12-digit) — required
- Marketplace Admin email(s) — must be able to accept offers
- Purchase Order referencing private offer ID (we will generate)
- Initial PO amount and chosen SKU

I created the private-offer draft in our internal track (DocuSign link below) — once Acme confirms the admin emails we’ll push the offer to AWS and share the acceptance flow.
